outline.description: This chapter introduces the parties, explains the premium financing arrangement between the insureds and APAC, describes the cancellation process at issue, and traces the procedural history from state court filing through removal and summary judgment.
subtopics: The parties: Williams, Wright, Jenkins, GoAuto, and APAC
Premium financing agreements and APAC's power of attorney
The underlying accident and policy cancellations for nonpayment
Procedural history: state court filing, removal to federal court, and cross-motions for summary judgment
The district court's ruling and dismissal with prejudice

outline.chapter_title: Louisiana's Statutory Framework for Policy Cancellation
outline.description: This chapter explains the Louisiana statute governing cancellation of financed insurance policies, the strict adherence standard required by Louisiana courts, the four certification elements, and the policy reasons behind requiring strict compliance.
subtopics: Text and structure of La. Rev. Stat. § 9:3550(G)(3)
The four certification requirements under § 9:3550(G)(3)(a)(i)–(iv)
The 'receipt' requirement under § 9:3550(G)(3)(b)(i)
Strict adherence standard from Louisiana case law (Delatte, Eaglin, Britten)
Policy purposes: fixing time of cancellation and providing cure period

outline.chapter_title: The Certification Issue: Whether a Signature is Required
outline.description: This chapter analyzes the plaintiffs' argument that certification requires a signature, examines the statutory text and relevant case law including Benitez, and explains the court's reasoning that companies can certify information without identifying a named individual.
subtopics: Plaintiffs' argument for a signature requirement based on the term 'certifying'
Absence of explicit signature requirement in the statutory text
Analysis of KMJ Services, Hodges, and other Louisiana precedent
Distinguishing Benitez v. Elsayed: signature discussed but not held dispositive
Court's holding that the finance company itself certifies, not a named employee

outline.chapter_title: The Receipt Requirement and Modern Technology
outline.description: This chapter examines whether GoAuto properly 'received' cancellation requests, including the definition of 'receipt' from Black's Law Dictionary, the mechanics of the electronic cancellation system, and how modern computer-based processes satisfy statutory requirements.
subtopics: Plaintiffs' argument that 'receipt' requires physical possession before cancellation
Statutory distinction between 'sending' and 'receipt'
Dictionary definitions of 'receipt' and 'receive'
GoAuto's computer system and the web service 'listener' mechanism
Court's holding that electronic receipt by computer system satisfies the statute

outline.chapter_title: Certification to the Louisiana Supreme Court and Final Disposition
outline.description: This chapter addresses the plaintiffs' request to certify the statutory interpretation questions to the Louisiana Supreme Court, explains the Fifth Circuit's standard for certification, and concludes with the court's final holding and disposition.
subtopics: Plaintiffs' certification request and arguments for importance to Louisiana insurance industry
Fifth Circuit's standard for certification (Jefferson v. Lead Industry Ass'n)
Court's rationale for declining certification
Summary of the court's conclusions on both disputed issues
Final disposition: affirmance of summary judgment for GoAuto
